findings.issue_text: [High/bug] apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx (formSchema ~l.48 and credentials submit handler ~l.120-160): `backupCode` was added to `LoginValues` but the zod `formSchema` was never extended (zodResolver strips unknown keys) and nothing forwards `backupCode` in the `signIn('credentials')` payload, so the backup code entered on the 'lost access' screen is never sent; the provider falls into the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`, which the handler swallows by re-setting `twoFactorRequired` — no error is shown and backup-code login can never succeed

[Medium/concurrency] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131-155: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read → `indexOf` → set `null` → full-array overwrite; two concurrent sign-ins with the same code both succeed, and concurrent sign-ins with different codes clobber each other's writes, resurrecting an already-consumed code and breaking the 'exactly once' guarantee; the code is also burned before `authorize` finishes, so a later failure consumes it without a successful login; use a transactional/conditional update or per-code rows consumed atomically

[Medium/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:60 + apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json: There is no way to generate/regenerate backup codes for an account that already has 2FA enabled — codes are only created during setup (which requires 2FA off), `disable` wipes them, and they are displayed exactly once with no re-view endpoint; users who enabled 2FA before this migration (`backupCodes` = null) and anyone who loses the one-time display can never obtain codes, yet the `missing_backup_codes` copy says 'Please generate them in your settings', a feature that doesn't exist

[Medium/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:219-262: After a successful enable, `onEnable()` fires only from the 'Close' button; dismissing the dialog at the `DisplayBackupCodes` step via X/Esc/overlay (`onOpenChange`) skips both `onEnable` and `resetState`, so the parent's 2FA switch keeps showing 'disabled' while 2FA is enabled server-side, and stale modal state persists for the next open

[Medium/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:60-62 (same pattern in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139): Backup-code verification is an exact, un-trimmed, case-sensitive string comparison while the input placeholder 'XXXXX-XXXXX' invites uppercase and the TextField sets no `autoCapitalize='none'` — mobile sentence auto-capitalization or uppercase manual entry will be wrongly rejected (codes are lowercase hex); normalize (trim + lowercase) on both ends

[Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-51: `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts the truthiness of the Promise object itself, so it always passes and the '2FA enabled' verification never checks anything; should be `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`

[Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12: No automated coverage for the PR's core new flows — login with a backup code, disabling 2FA with a backup code, single-use consumption, or the `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes` paths; the downloaded file content and clipboard content are also unasserted

[Low/bug] apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:118: Cancel (`onCancel`) doesn't reset `twoFactorLostAccess` (or `errorMessage`), so reopening the modal later starts in the backup-code view with stale error state; only the success path resets

[Low/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:68-72: `resetState()` doesn't call `form.reset()` (a previously entered `totpCode` can prefill the next enable attempt), doesn't clear `backupCodes`/`dataUri`/`secret`, and never revokes the `backupCodesUrl` blob URL on close, leaking an object URL each time the flow runs

[Low/security] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:60-66: Backup codes are stored reversibly encrypted (`symmetricEncrypt`) rather than hashed; they are only ever compared, so per-code hashing (as with passwords) would render them useless to an attacker who obtains both the database and `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx (formSchema ~l.48 and credentials submit handler ~l.120-160): `backupCode` was added to `LoginValues` but the zod `formSchema` was never extended (zodResolver strips unknown keys) and nothing forwards `backupCode` in the `signIn('credentials')` payload, so the backup code entered on the 'lost access' screen is never sent; the provider falls into the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`, which the handler swallows by re-setting `twoFactorRequired` — no error is shown and backup-code login can never succeed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `backupCode` to `LoginValues` and introduces a UI path that renders `<BackupCode />`, which registers `backupCode` via `useFormContext()` (`methods.register("backupCode")`). However, in the shown changes to `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`, there is no corresponding change visible to (a) extend the existing Zod `formSchema` used by `zodResolver` to include `backupCode`, nor (b) ensure the `signIn('credentials', ...)` submission payload includes `backupCode`. Given Zod object parsing typically drops unknown keys, this would prevent `backupCode` from being sent, making the new “lost access” login path non-functional. (The exact schema and sign-in call aren’t in the provided diff hunks, so this is inferred from the absence of any related modifications.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:60 + apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json: There is no way to generate/regenerate backup codes for an account that already has 2FA enabled — codes are only created during setup (which requires 2FA off), `disable` wipes them, and they are displayed exactly once with no re-view endpoint; users who enabled 2FA before this migration (`backupCodes` = null) and anyone who loses the one-time display can never obtain codes, yet the `missing_backup_codes` copy says 'Please generate them in your settings', a feature that doesn't exist

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows backup codes are generated only in `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` (now returns `backupCodes`), displayed once in `EnableTwoFactorModal` (new `DisplayBackupCodes` step), and then wiped on disable (`disable.ts` sets `backupCodes: null`). The new error string `missing_backup_codes` tells users to “generate them in your settings”, but this diff does not add any regenerate/review mechanism beyond the one-time display during enable. That’s a concrete completeness/UX gap (especially for users with `backupCodes = null`), though not an outright functional defect provable to break existing flows from this diff alone because regeneration might exist elsewhere in the codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:219-262: After a successful enable, `onEnable()` fires only from the 'Close' button; dismissing the dialog at the `DisplayBackupCodes` step via X/Esc/overlay (`onOpenChange`) skips both `onEnable` and `resetState`, so the parent's 2FA switch keeps showing 'disabled' while 2FA is enabled server-side, and stale modal state persists for the next open

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, a successful enable now does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` (no `onEnable()` call). At the DisplayBackupCodes step, the only code path that calls `onEnable()`/`resetState()` is the explicit Close button (`data-testid="backup-codes-close"`). The Dialog’s `onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` is passed through without wrapping to also call `resetState()` and/or `onEnable()` when the dialog is dismissed via X/Esc/overlay, so closing that way can leave the parent uninformed (2FA enabled server-side but UI switch not updated) and the modal state (step/backup codes) stale on next open.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-51: `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts the truthiness of the Promise object itself, so it always passes and the '2FA enabled' verification never checks anything; should be `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts the code does `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();`. `locator.isChecked()` returns a Promise<boolean>, and the Promise object itself is always truthy, so this assertion does not actually verify the checkbox state. The diff even adds a FIXME noting this behavior. The correct Playwright assertion would be `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` (or `await expect(locator.isChecked()).resolves.toBeTruthy()`).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new backup-code flows (login supports `backupCode` in `next-auth-options.ts` authorize; disable endpoint `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` accepts `backupCode` and adds `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes`; UI toggles between TOTP and `<BackupCode/>` in `login.tsx` and `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx`). The Playwright test changes in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` only add a TODO comment and basic clicks for download/copy/close, but explicitly leave file content and clipboard content unasserted (`// TODO: check file content`, `// TODO: check clipboard content`) and do not cover backup-code login, disabling 2FA via backup code, or single-use consumption/error paths. This is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:118: Cancel (`onCancel`) doesn't reset `twoFactorLostAccess` (or `errorMessage`), so reopening the modal later starts in the backup-code view with stale error state; only the success path resets

adjudication.rationale: In DisableTwoFactorModal, twoFactorLostAccess and errorMessage are component state. The success path explicitly does `setTwoFactorLostAccess(false); resetForm();` (handleDisable). But the Cancel button just calls `onCancel` without resetting either state (`<Button ... onClick={onCancel}>`). If the modal is closed via `onCancel` and later reopened without unmounting the component (common with controlled dialogs), it will reopen with the previous view (backup-code vs TOTP) and/or stale error text. The diff shows no reset on cancel/close besides the success path and the lost_access toggle handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:60-66: Backup codes are stored reversibly encrypted (`symmetricEncrypt`) rather than hashed; they are only ever compared, so per-code hashing (as with passwords) would render them useless to an attacker who obtains both the database and `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`

adjudication.rationale: The diff does store backup codes using reversible encryption: in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` it saves `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)`, and later code paths decrypt and compare (`next-auth-options.ts` and `totp/disable.ts` use `symmetricDecrypt(...)` then `indexOf(...)`). Since the codes are only used for equality checks, hashing (e.g., per-code salted hash) is a reasonable security hardening suggestion. However, this is not a clear functional defect in the diff (encryption-at-rest is still a valid approach); it’s a design/security improvement request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the password visibility toggle button in `PasswordField` (`packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx`) to `tabIndex={-1}`. This removes the control from the keyboard tab order everywhere `PasswordField` is used, which is an accessibility/keyboard-navigation regression (users can no longer reach the show/hide password toggle via Tab). adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:58: `useState([])` infers `never[]` for `backupCodes`, so the values rendered, formatted, copied, and downloaded have no real typing on a security-sensitive field; use `useState<string[]>([])`

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` the diff adds `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);` (around where other state hooks are declared). With TS/React, `useState([])` commonly infers `never[]` (or otherwise an unhelpfully broad type), so the later usage `backupCodes.map((code) => formatBackupCode(code))` and `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` lacks meaningful typing for what should be `string[]`. This is a type-safety issue rather than a runtime defect, and can be fixed by `useState<string[]>([])`.
